comment:
Nice and caring professor. As an Econ major, I struggled to interpret the weekly readings in the way he expected. Very engaging and expects participation. 

His feedback was broad, even though he had specific criteria in mind. The course itself is interesting and engaging. Understanding his grading expectations early is important for a good grade.

This professor is a very nice person and very caring. The essays require a lot of work but if you do them right it is not super difficult to get an A. I am not a history major, but I still enjoyed this class and hope to take another class with him.
Really nice professor. Course may require heavy reading but professor is super nice

No tests or quizzes, jist essays; have the option to do a creative essay or an analysis for the final; must write a response every week based on the readings; second half of semester much more enjoyable then first; comes off as demeaning at times and can make you feel dumb at times but it seems he is not aware of it/does it intentionally
Alright guy,  clearly a very knowledgeable person. Dont recommend this class as its a FYS class and his assignments and grading criteria were far too harsh for a first year, first semester class.

Ignore the bad reviews… honestly anyone who can't appreciate what a brilliant professor baker is does not deserve to experience one of his classes. Genuinely you will learn so much in his classes. Baker will always challenge you and this will help you grow as a Historian. If you can't accept criticism then you aren't gonna grow

Shocked at some of the positive comments about Baker. While he isn't the worst professor I have had he is very patronizing and his class is far too difficult for an FYS class. This is more like a junior level history class from what I have experienced taking other History classes, Baker grades the papers with similar criteria.

Do not take this class, ignore the misleading comments. When comparing this FYS class to others the workload and strict grading criteria make it by far the worst FYS class to take. Prepare for high standards especially for 1st years when taking this class

I recommend taking the Silk Roads FYS class if you enjoy condescending and strict graders. Baker had weekly journals meant to introduce 1st-year students to writing and graded them very harshly, along with giving more homework than other FYS classes. Take a different FYS class or you will look back at this comment and regret it.

Professor Baker is the best professor I have ever taken a class with. He is extremely kind and passionate about his teaching. He is always there for students when they have questions or need help. He is rather funny and fun to listen to in classes and lectures

Dr. Baker is a thoughtful, supportive professor who genuinely cares about his students. While the content may not engage everyone, he works hard to make it interesting and is highly knowledgeable. He provides valuable feedback, is accessible and kind, and is well-organized, offering clear structure and opportunities for improvement.
Weekly journals are usually graded on completion, but he graded them so harshly based on your grammar and analytics skills.
